# CSV export for the invoice list — plan

Verify command: `sh verify.sh` (healthy output ends with `N passed, 0 failed`)

## Files to change
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `bin/invoices` | Parse `--csv` (any position, combinable with `--status`). When set, print the header and rows as CSV instead of the table. Phase 2 loads `lib/csv.awk` and routes each field through `csv_field`. Update the usage comment and usage message. |
| `lib/csv.awk` (new, phase 2) | The `csv_field(s)` function and nothing else. |
| `tests/test_csv.sh` (new) | Checks for AC1–AC4 and, in Test, AC5. `verify.sh` already runs every `tests/test_*.sh`, so no wiring is needed. It uses `check` from `tests/lib.sh`. |

No other file changes. No new dependency, fixture file or config option.

## Phases
| # | Phase | Covers | Depends on | First failing test | Runs in | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CSV output, no quoting | AC1, AC2, AC4, PR 1 in the RFC | — | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv prints the header and four rows` | main session | in_progress |
| 2 | Quoting | AC3, PR 2 in the RFC | 1 | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv quotes commas and doubles quotes` | main session | pending |

Status is `pending`, `in_progress` or `done`. One phase is in progress per session or worktree.

### Phase 1 — CSV output, no quoting
Start with `tests/test_csv.sh`. Before touching `bin/invoices`, add the AC4 check: `bin/invoices list` output equals the table captured from the current code (an inline `printf` of the five table lines, copied from running the unchanged script). It passes at once, and it must stay green through both phases. Then add the AC1 check and watch it fail.

In `bin/invoices`, add `csv=0` and a `--csv) csv=1; shift ;;` case to the option loop. After the loop, when `csv=1`, run the same awk filter as the table (`NR == 1 || status == "" || $4 == status`) but print `$1,$2,$3,$4` joined with commas and a newline. The header is row 1 of the data file, so it prints as `id,customer,amount,status` with no special case. Use `awk -F '\t'` and print fields as they are (amounts stay strings, per CLAUDE.md). Keep the table branch exactly as it is. Output uses `\n` line endings; the spec doesn't ask for RFC 4180's CRLF (see Open points).

Checks for this phase: AC1 (header line is exactly `id,customer,amount,status`, total 5 lines, and the first data row is exactly `INV-001,Northwind Traders,1200.00,open`), AC2 (`--status open --csv` and `--csv --status open` both give the header plus 3 lines, all with status `open`), AC4.

### Phase 2 — Quoting
Add the AC3 check first (the two exact rows `INV-002,"Acme, Inc.",310.50,paid` and `INV-004,"Initech ""West""",4500.00,open`) and watch it fail, because phase 1 prints them unquoted.

Create `lib/csv.awk` holding one function: `csv_field(s)` returns `s` unchanged unless it contains `,` or `"`; otherwise it does `gsub(/"/, "\"\"", s)` and returns `"\"" s "\""`. In `bin/invoices`, load it by putting its text in front of the CSV awk program: `awk -F '\t' "$(cat "$root/lib/csv.awk")
<program>"`. Reason: awk can't mix `-f file` with an inline program, and this is plain POSIX with no `/dev/stdin` dependency. I checked on this machine's awk (version 20200816) that both this form and `-f lib/csv.awk -f /dev/stdin` work. The CSV branch then prints `csv_field($1) "," csv_field($2) ...` for each field. This keeps the RFC's chosen design (option A, quoting in `lib/csv.awk`) and only changes how the file is loaded. If that load fails on the CI image, the RFC's fallback applies: move the function inline into `bin/invoices`.

## Todos
### Phase 1 — CSV output, no quoting
- [ ] Create `tests/test_csv.sh`, add the AC4 check against the current table output, run `sh verify.sh` and confirm it passes
- [ ] Add the AC1 check `--csv prints the header and four rows` and watch it fail
- [ ] Add `--csv` to `bin/invoices` until AC1 passes
- [ ] Add the AC2 check (both option orders), watch it fail or confirm it passes for the right reason, then fix
- [ ] Refactor, run `sh verify.sh`, and run pr-review `--local`

## Tests
Build writes each Build test before the code it tests. Test writes the final tests, which need the whole feature.

The testing toolkit isn't installed on this machine, and the Goldfish review wasn't run (EGM isn't installed either). I chose and sorted these tests by hand. Lee should check this section.

- Scenario: a command-line tool that prints text from a data file. The tests run the real `bin/invoices` and compare its exact output. Done when: every acceptance criterion has a check that fails without the change and passes with it, and `sh verify.sh` ends with `0 failed`.
- Left out: unit tests of `csv_field` on its own — the function has one caller, and AC3 reaches it through the real command; a separate harness would be more code than the function.
- Left out: a quoting check for fields with a newline — the data is tab-separated, one record per line, so a field can't contain one.
- Left out: a test that the `--csv` flag appears in the usage message — the spec doesn't require it.

| Acceptance criterion | Test | Kind | Written in | Where the bug would be |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC1 | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv prints the header and four rows` | integration (real command, sample data) | Build, phase 1 | the header, and the field order and separators |
| AC2 | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv --status open prints the header and three open rows` | integration | Build, phase 1 | the `--csv` and `--status` options interacting, in either order |
| AC3 | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv quotes commas and doubles quotes` | integration | Build, phase 2 | `csv_field` and the way `bin/invoices` loads `lib/csv.awk` |
| AC4 | `tests/test_csv.sh::list without --csv is unchanged` | regression (exact bytes) | Build, phase 1 (written first, passes at once) | the table branch, which the new option parsing touches |
| AC5 | `tests/test_csv.sh::2000 invoices export in under 5 seconds` | performance | Test | the hot path: one awk pass over a generated 2,000-row `INVOICES_FILE` |

The AC5 test generates its file with awk into a `mktemp` path, cleans it up, and times the command with `date +%s` before and after. One-second resolution is enough for a 5-second limit.

## Risk and size
- **Riskiest step:** phase 2's loading of `lib/csv.awk`, because the RFC's fallback names it. It is covered by AC3. The `cat` form is plain POSIX, and the fallback remains.
- **Not caught by the tests:** line endings (CRLF versus LF) in a spreadsheet, and customer names with leading or trailing spaces. Neither is in the spec.
- **Size check:** one new source file (`lib/csv.awk`, required by the RFC), one new test file (`verify.sh` picks it up through its glob), no dependency, no config option, no fixture file (expected output is inline). Nothing was cut that the spec requires.

## Open points for Lee
- Line endings: the plan emits `\n`. RFC 4180 says CRLF. The spec's R3 cites RFC 4180 only for quoting. Say so if you want CRLF, and AC1 and AC3 would then need `\r`.
- Loading mechanism: the plan deviates slightly from the RFC's `awk -f` wording (see Phase 2), with the same design.

# CSV export for the invoice list — plan

Verify command: `sh verify.sh` (healthy output ends with `N passed, 0 failed`)

## Files to change
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `bin/invoices` | Parse a `--csv` flag. When it's set, the awk step prints CSV rows instead of the padded table. The filter is unchanged. Without `--csv`, the table `printf` is untouched. |
| `lib/csv.awk` (new, phase 2) | Holds the `csv_field(s)` function. |
| `tests/test_list.sh` | Adds the byte-exact table check for AC4. |
| `tests/test_csv.sh` (new) | Holds the CSV checks for AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5. `verify.sh` picks it up through its `tests/test_*.sh` glob. |

No dependency, no config option, no other new file. `data/invoices.tsv` already has the header row and the two rows that need quoting (`Acme, Inc.` and `Initech "West"`), so there is no new fixture. AC5 generates its 2,000-invoice file at test time.

## Phases
| # | Phase | Covers | Depends on | First failing test | Runs in | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CSV output, no quoting | AC1, AC2, AC4, PR 1 in the RFC | — | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv prints the header and four rows` | main session | in_progress |
| 2 | Quoting | AC3, PR 2 in the RFC | 1 | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv quotes commas and doubles quotes` | main session | pending |

Status is `pending`, `in_progress` or `done`. One phase is in progress per session or worktree.

### Phase 1 — CSV output, no quoting
Before any code, add the AC4 check to `tests/test_list.sh`. It compares the full output of `bin/invoices list` to the literal expected bytes, which are the current output of the base commit (header plus four rows, padded `%-8s %-22s %10s  %s`). It must pass now and keep passing, which proves the table doesn't change.

Then write the AC1 and AC2 checks in the new `tests/test_csv.sh` and watch them fail (`--csv` today exits 2 with "unknown option"):
- `--csv prints the header and four rows`: `bin/invoices list --csv` has exactly 5 lines and the first is `id,customer,amount,status`.
- `--csv --status open prints the header and three rows`: `bin/invoices list --status open --csv` has 4 lines, with the header first. Also run it as `--csv --status open`, because option order must not matter.

Implementation in `bin/invoices`: add `csv=0` next to `status=""`, and add a case arm `--csv) csv=1; shift ;;`. Pass `-v csv="$csv"` to awk. In the awk body keep the existing condition `NR == 1 || status == "" || $4 == status` and branch inside it: when `csv` is `1`, print `$1 "," $2 "," $3 "," $4` (fields as strings, never as numbers, per CLAUDE.md), otherwise run the existing `printf`. Row 1 is the data file's header, which already reads `id customer amount status`, so it becomes the CSV header without special-casing. Update the usage comment and usage message to show `[--csv]`.

This phase writes no quoting, so `Acme, Inc.` comes out unquoted. That is expected until phase 2.

### Phase 2 — Quoting
Write the AC3 check first and watch it fail. In `tests/test_csv.sh`, `--csv quotes commas and doubles quotes` asserts that the output contains the exact lines `INV-002,"Acme, Inc.",310.50,paid` and `INV-004,"Initech ""West""",4500.00,open` (`grep -Fx` each). Also assert that `INV-001,Northwind Traders,1200.00,open` stays unquoted, so the function doesn't quote everything.

Create `lib/csv.awk` with one function:

```awk
function csv_field(s) {
  if (s ~ /[",]/) { gsub(/"/, "\"\"", s); return "\"" s "\"" }
  return s
}
```

In `bin/invoices`, load it by prepending its text to the awk program, not with a second `-f`, because POSIX awk can't mix `-f` with an inline program. Keep the program in a shell variable `prog` and run `awk -F '\t' -v ... "$(cat "$root/lib/csv.awk")
$prog" "$data"`. In the CSV branch, print `csv_field($1) "," csv_field($2) "," csv_field($3) "," csv_field($4)`. This keeps the RFC's chosen layout (quoting lives in `lib/csv.awk`) and makes the RFC's fallback unnecessary, because the file's text is concatenated rather than passed with `-f`. Run the whole verify command, so the AC4 check proves the table is still unchanged.

## Todos
Only a phase that's in progress has todos here. Build writes the next phase's todos when it starts that phase.

### Phase 1 — CSV output, no quoting
- [ ] Add the byte-exact table check (AC4) to `tests/test_list.sh` and confirm it passes on the unchanged code
- [ ] Write the failing tests `--csv prints the header and four rows` and `--csv --status open prints the header and three rows` in `tests/test_csv.sh` and watch them fail
- [ ] Add the `--csv` flag and the CSV branch to `bin/invoices` until both pass
- [ ] Refactor, run `sh verify.sh`, and run pr-review

## Tests
Build writes each Build test before the code it tests. Test writes the final tests, which need the whole feature.

- Scenario: a small shell CLI change with an unchanged default path. Each AC is a black-box check of `bin/invoices` output, which is the same level at which Finance uses it. Done when: each AC has a passing `check` line in `sh verify.sh`, and the AC4 check passes both before and after the change.
- Left out: unit test of `csv_field` on its own — the awk function has no entry point outside `bin/invoices`, and AC3 covers its two branches (quoted, unquoted) through the CLI.
- Left out: fuzz or property tests of the quoting — the rule is two cases, and AC3 uses both real sample rows.
- Left out: formal verification — no concurrency, state or protocol claim in the RFC.
- Left out: CSV fields with embedded newlines — the TSV input can't contain them, and the spec doesn't ask for them.

| Acceptance criterion | Test | Kind | Written in | Where the bug would be |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC1 | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv prints the header and four rows` | integration (CLI output) | Build, phase 1 | The flag parsing, and the CSV branch of the awk step |
| AC2 | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv --status open prints the header and three rows` | integration (CLI output) | Build, phase 1 | The `--csv` flag combined with `--status`, in either order |
| AC3 | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv quotes commas and doubles quotes` | integration (CLI output) | Build, phase 2 | `csv_field`'s regex and the doubling of inner quotes |
| AC4 | `tests/test_list.sh::list output is byte-identical to the base` | regression (golden output) | Build, phase 1 | The default branch of the awk step, which the CSV branch shares |
| AC5 | `tests/test_csv.sh::--csv exports 2000 invoices in under 5 seconds` | performance | Test | The hot path, if the quoting function runs once per field of 2,000 rows. It generates the 2,000-row file in `$TMPDIR` and times the command with `date +%s`. |

## Risks and open points for Lee
- **PR 1 alone emits malformed CSV** for `Acme, Inc.` and `Initech "West"`, because quoting only arrives in PR 2. Nobody should announce `--csv` to Finance until PR 2 merges. If that is a worry, merge the two PRs together or hold PR 1 until PR 2 is ready.
- **Concatenating `lib/csv.awk` into the program text** differs slightly from the RFC's `awk -f` wording, though the layout is the same. I chose it because POSIX awk can't combine `-f` with an inline program. If the awk program grows, moving the main program into its own file and using two `-f` flags is the next step.
- **The AC5 timing** has one-second granularity, which is fine for a 5-second limit. It can still be flaky on a loaded CI machine.
- **Reviewed without tools:** EGM and the testing toolkit aren't installed here, so there is no Goldfish review and the tests were chosen by hand, which `sdlc.yaml` records.

# Plan: CSV export for the invoice list

Feature: csv-export. Implements the approved [RFC](rfc.md) against the approved [spec](spec.md).
Owner: Sam. Approver: Lee.

## Approach
Two PRs, in the order the RFC sets. Each PR leaves `sh verify.sh` green and can be reverted on its own.

- **PR 1 (REP-101):** `bin/invoices list --csv` prints the header and the rows, with no quoting yet.
- **PR 2 (REP-102):** `lib/csv.awk` and its `csv_field` function quote the fields, and `--csv` uses it.

The table path (the existing inline awk program) is never edited. `--csv` is a separate branch in `bin/invoices`, so R4 holds by construction, and a fixture test checks it.

## Design notes
- `awk` takes either `-f` files or an inline program, not both. The RFC's "two program files" therefore means:
  - `lib/csv.awk` holds only `csv_field`.
  - A second file, `lib/list_csv.awk`, holds the row-printing program.
  - `bin/invoices` runs `awk -F '\t' -v status="$status" -f "$root/lib/csv.awk" -f "$root/lib/list_csv.awk" "$data"`.
  - In PR 1, before `csv.awk` exists, the CSV branch runs `-f "$root/lib/list_csv.awk"` alone.
- The header row is printed literally as `id,customer,amount,status` in `BEGIN`, and the file's own first row is skipped. A filter that matches nothing still prints the header, as the table does.
- The filter is the same as the table's: `status == "" || $4 == status`.
- Amounts are printed as the untouched `$3` string. No `printf "%f"`, no `+0`. (CLAUDE.md: amounts are decimal strings.)
- The usage text in `bin/invoices` gains `[--csv]`. It goes to stderr, so no stdout output changes.

## PR 1: `--csv` output (REP-101)
Covers R1, R2, R4, AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5.

Steps:
1. **Before editing `bin/invoices`**, capture the current table output as fixtures, so AC4 compares against the pre-change bytes:
   - `bin/invoices list > tests/fixtures/list.expected`
   - `bin/invoices list --status open > tests/fixtures/list_open.expected`
2. Add `lib/list_csv.awk`. It prints the header in `BEGIN`, skips `NR == 1`, applies the status filter, and prints `$1,$2,$3,$4` joined with commas.
3. In `bin/invoices`, add a `--csv` case to the option loop that sets `csv=1`. After parsing, run the CSV branch when `csv=1`, and otherwise the existing awk program, unchanged. Update the usage line.
4. Add `tests/test_csv.sh` and `tests/test_perf.sh` (below).

Tests (3 existing + 10 new = 13 expected):

| # | Check | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--csv` first line is exactly `id,customer,amount,status` | R1 |
| 2 | `--csv` prints the header and four rows (5 lines) | AC1 |
| 3 | `--status open --csv` prints the header and three rows (4 lines) | AC2 |
| 4 | `--csv --status open` and `--status open --csv` print identical output | R2 |
| 5 | `--status nope --csv` prints the header only (1 line) | R2 edge |
| 6 | `bin/invoices list` equals `tests/fixtures/list.expected` (`cmp`) | AC4 |
| 7 | `bin/invoices list --status open` equals `tests/fixtures/list_open.expected` | AC4 |
| 8 | A temp file with amounts `0.10` and `12345678901234567.89` exports them unchanged | CLAUDE.md convention |
| 9 | A 2,000-invoice export prints 2,001 lines | AC5 |
| 10 | The same export finishes in under 5 seconds | AC5 |

Notes on the tests:
- Checks 6 and 7 compare bytes with `cmp`, not line counts, because AC4 is about bytes.
- `tests/test_perf.sh` builds the 2,000-invoice file with awk into a `mktemp` file and removes it with a `trap`. It sets `INVOICES_FILE` for the run. Every tenth customer name has a comma and every twentieth has a double quote, so the file still exercises the quoting path in PR 2.
- Elapsed time uses `date +%s`, which has 1-second resolution. That is enough for a 5-second limit. Expect well under 1 second.
- Tests follow the existing style: `check "name" 'command'` from `tests/lib.sh`. Quote-heavy expectations go in fixture files, because `check` runs its command through `eval`, and nested double quotes get fragile.

Done when `sh verify.sh` ends with `13 passed, 0 failed`.

## PR 2: quoting (REP-102)
Covers R3, AC3.

Steps:
1. Add `lib/csv.awk` with `csv_field(s)`. If `s` contains `,` or `"`, it doubles every `"` with `gsub(/"/, "\"\"", s)` and returns the result wrapped in double quotes. Otherwise it returns `s` unchanged.
2. In `lib/list_csv.awk`, pass `$2` through `csv_field`. Apply it to all four fields, so the rule is uniform. Only the customer can contain these characters today, but the function is cheap.
3. In `bin/invoices`, add `-f "$root/lib/csv.awk"` ahead of `list_csv.awk`.
4. Add the golden fixture `tests/fixtures/export.expected` (the full expected CSV for the sample data) and four checks to `tests/test_csv.sh`.

Tests (13 + 4 new = 17 expected):

| # | Check | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | The export contains the line `INV-002,"Acme, Inc.",310.50,paid` | AC3 |
| 12 | The export contains the line `INV-004,"Initech ""West""",4500.00,open` | AC3 |
| 13 | The full export of the sample data equals `tests/fixtures/export.expected` (`cmp`) | R1, R3 |
| 14 | A customer with both a comma and a quote, `a, "b"`, exports as `"a, ""b"""` | R3 edge |

The existing checks 1 to 10 must still pass. Checks 9 and 10 now run the quoted path on the 2,000-invoice file, so AC5 is re-verified with quoting on.

Done when `sh verify.sh` ends with `17 passed, 0 failed`.

## Fallback
If `awk -f a -f b` behaves differently on the CI image, apply the RFC's fallback. Move `csv_field` and the row program inline into `bin/invoices` (option B). The tests don't change, because they exercise only the command's output.

## Risks
| Risk | Detection | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| The table output changes | Checks 6 and 7 (byte comparison with the pre-change fixtures) | Fixtures are captured before `bin/invoices` is edited. Revert the PR. |
| Quoting is wrong for a field with both characters | Checks 11 to 14 | None needed beyond the tests. |
| Amounts get reformatted by awk number handling | Check 8 | Print `$3` as a string, never do arithmetic on it. |
| Multiple `-f` files differ on the CI image | `sh verify.sh` on CI | The RFC fallback above. |

## Out of scope
Per the spec: scheduled exports, Excel format. Also not handled: fields that contain newlines. The TSV format can't hold them, so the spec's comma-and-quote rule is complete for this input.

## Open questions
- None.

   }

# CSV export for the invoice list — spec

Risk: low
Policies applied: none (no security, compliance, brand, UX or API policy skills are loaded in this session; `CLAUDE.md` convention "amounts are decimal strings" applied as R4)

## Summary
`bin/invoices list` gains a `--format csv` option. It prints the same invoices the plain listing would, as RFC 4180 CSV that a spreadsheet opens directly. Finance redirects the output to a file instead of copying the table by hand. The default output is unchanged.

## Requirements
- **R1** `bin/invoices list --format csv` prints the invoice table as CSV to stdout, one record per line, with the header row `id,customer,amount,status` first.
- **R2** `--format csv` combines with `--status open|paid`. The output holds the header plus only the invoices with that status, in the same order as `data/invoices.tsv`.
- **R3** A field that contains a comma or a double quote is written inside double quotes, and each double quote inside it is doubled. Example: `Acme, Inc.` becomes `"Acme, Inc."` and `Initech "West"` becomes `"Initech ""West"""`.
- **R4** The amount is copied byte for byte from the data file. The export doesn't reformat, round or convert it.
- **R5** Records end with CRLF, as RFC 4180 specifies.
- **R6** `--format` with any value other than `csv` or `table` prints `unknown format: <value>` to stderr and exits 2, with no stdout. `--format table` produces the existing output.
- **R7** Without `--format`, the output of `bin/invoices list` is byte-identical to today's, with and without `--status`.
- **R8** The export reads from `INVOICES_FILE` when set, the same as `list` does today.
- **R9** The change adds no dependency beyond POSIX shell and awk.

## Non-functional requirements
- Performance: exporting 2,000 invoices finishes in under 5 seconds on the machine `sh verify.sh` runs on.
- Compatibility: runs under `sh` (POSIX) and a POSIX-conforming awk. No GNU-only awk extensions.
- The export only reads the data file. It writes nothing except stdout and stderr.

| Id | Criterion | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | On the sample `data/invoices.tsv`, `bin/invoices list --format csv` prints a header `id,customer,amount,status` followed by four records, one per invoice. | R1 |
| AC2 | `bin/invoices list --format csv --status paid` prints the header and only INV-002. `--status open` prints the header and INV-001, INV-003, INV-004 in that order. | R2 |
| AC3 | The INV-002 record's customer field is `"Acme, Inc."` and the INV-004 record's is `"Initech ""West"""`. Parsing the output with a CSV reader returns the original customer names. | R3 |
| AC4 | Given a data file whose amount is `0012.50`, the CSV amount field is `0012.50`. | R4 |
| AC5 | Every line of the output ends with `\r\n`, checked with `od -c`. | R5 |
| AC6 | `--format xml` exits 2, prints `unknown format: xml` on stderr and prints nothing on stdout. `--format table` output equals the output without the flag. | R6 |
| AC7 | `bin/invoices list` and `bin/invoices list --status open` produce the same bytes before and after the change, compared against output captured from the base commit. | R7 |
| AC8 | With `INVOICES_FILE` pointing at a different file, the CSV holds that file's rows. | R8 |
| AC9 | The diff adds no file outside `bin/invoices`, `tests/` and `docs/`, and `bin/invoices` calls only `sh` builtins and `awk`. | R9 |

| Concern | Policy owner | Resolution |
|---|---|---|

- Fields are separated by commas. Records end with CRLF (RFC 4180).
- A field is wrapped in double quotes if it contains a comma, a double quote, a CR or an LF. Inside a quoted field every double quote is doubled. Other fields are written bare.

- Implemented in POSIX shell and awk in `bin/invoices`. No new dependencies.
- One awk pass over the file, with the existing row filter shared with `list` so the two cannot drift apart. The CSV quoting is a small awk function that doubles quotes and wraps the field when needed.
